# Jubilees Chapter 7 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QJub (Hebrew fragments) | **Section:** Noah's Vineyard; Canaan's Sin; Curses and Blessings; Division of the Earth

---

**7:1** In the seventh year of this week Noah planted a vineyard on the mountain where the ark had rested — Mount Lubar, one of the Ararat mountains — and it bore fruit in the fourth year. He guarded its fruit and gathered it in the seventh month of that year.

**7:2** He made wine from it and put it into a vessel, and kept it until the fifth year, until the first day of the first month.

**7:3** On that day he celebrated the feast with joy — he and his sons before him — and he drank of the wine on that day.

**7:4** Now on this day while Noah was celebrating and rejoicing, his sons before him, Canaan saw that his grandfather was drunk. He came and laid hold of him, mocked him, and did not cover his shame before him, but left him lying naked and went away.

**7:5** Ham, his father, saw the nakedness of Noah his father and went and told his two brothers outside.

**7:6** Shem and Japheth took a garment and both of them arose, walked backward, and covered their father's shame. Their faces were turned away and they did not see their father's nakedness.

**7:7** Noah awoke from his sleep and learned everything that his younger grandson had done to him, and he cursed his son and said: "Cursed be Canaan; an enslaved servant shall he be to his brothers."

**7:8** He blessed Shem and said: "Blessed be the LORD God of Shem, and may Canaan be his servant."

**7:9** "May God enlarge Japheth, and may God dwell in the tents of Shem. And may Canaan be his servant."

**7:10** Ham learned that his father had cursed his youngest son, and it grieved him greatly.

**7:11** Noah slept with his fathers and was buried on Mount Lubar in the land of Ararat.

**7:12** He lived three hundred and fifty years after the flood, and all the days of his life were nine hundred and fifty years, and he died.

**7:13** In his life on earth he excelled all the children of men except Enoch, because of the righteousness in which he was perfect. For Enoch's task was ordained as a testimony to the generations of the world, to recount all the deeds of generation after generation until the day of judgment.

**7:14** In the twenty-ninth jubilee, in the first week, in the beginning of it, Arpachshad took a wife named Rasu'eja, daughter of Susan daughter of Elam, and she bore him a son in the third year of that week, and he named him Kainam.

**7:15** The son grew, and his father taught him writing. He went out to find a place where he might take possession of a city for himself.

**7:16** He found an inscription which earlier generations had carved on a rock, and he read what was on it and transcribed it, and sinned because of it — for it contained the teaching of the Watchers by which they used to observe the omens of the sun, moon, and stars in all the signs of heaven.

**7:17** He copied it down and said nothing about it, for he feared that Noah would be angry with him if he were told.

**7:18** In the thirtieth jubilee, in the second week, in the first year, he took a wife named Melka, daughter of Madai son of Japheth, and in the fourth year he fathered a son whom he named Shelah; for he said: "Truly I have been sent."

**7:19** In the thirty-first jubilee, in the first week, in the second year, Shelah took a wife named Mu'ak, daughter of Kesed his father's brother.

**7:20** She bore him a son in the fifth year, and he named him Eber. Then Eber took a wife named 'Azurad, daughter of Nebrod, in the thirty-second jubilee, in the seventh week, in the third year.

**7:21** In the first year of the thirty-third jubilee she bore him a son, and he named him Peleg, for in the days of his birth the children of Noah began to divide the earth among themselves — that is why he was named Peleg.

**7:22** They divided it secretly among themselves and reported it to Noah.

**7:23** It came to pass at the beginning of the thirty-third jubilee that they divided the earth into three portions for Shem, Ham, and Japheth, according to the inheritance of each, in the first year of the first week, when one of us was sent to instruct them.

**7:24** Noah called his sons, and they came near — they and their children — and he distributed the earth by lot among his three sons. They reached forward and drew the lots from the bosom of Noah their father.

**7:25** The lot of Shem was the middle of the earth, which he should take as an inheritance for himself and for his sons forever — from the middle of the mountain range of Rafa, from the mouth of the water of the river Tina. His portion extends westward through the midst of this river until it reaches the waters of the abyss from which this river flows and pours into the sea Maat, which flows into the great sea.

**7:26** Everything to the north is Japheth's, and everything to the south belongs to Shem.

---
*SOPHIA notes: The key Jubilees variation — Canaan is the direct offender (v.4), not Ham — preserved clearly. "Tents of Shem" (v.9) follows LOGOS/Gen 9:27 echo. Kainam (vv.14-17) preserved as a Jubilees/LXX figure transmitting Watcher knowledge. Geographical descriptions (v.25) preserved literally.*
